question:
Red Star Plastic Factory produces 6 types of plastic containers, with their capacities, demands, and variable costs shown in Table 5-11.
Table 5-11
\begin{tabular}{c|c|c|c|c|c|c}
\hline Container Code & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 6 \
\hline Capacity $(\mathrm{cm}^3)$ & 1500 & 2500 & 4000 & 6000 & 9000 & 12000 \
Demand/units & 500 & 550 & 700 & 900 & 400 & 300 \
Variable Cost/(¥/unit) & 5 & 8 & 10 & 12 & 16 & 18 \
\hline
\end{tabular}

Each type of container is produced using different dedicated equipment, with a fixed cost of ¥1200. When the quantity of a certain container cannot meet the demand, containers with larger capacities can be used as substitutes. How should production be organized to minimize the total cost while meeting the demand?

candidates.code:
"""
Red Star Plastic Factory - production / substitution MILP

Decision variables
------------------
x[i, j] : integer, units of container type i produced to satisfy demand of type j
          (allowed only when capacity_i >= capacity_j, i.e. j <= i in the given
          ordering where capacity increases with index).
y[i]    : binary, 1 if equipment for container type i is run (fixed cost 1200).

Objective (minimize)
--------------------
sum_i fixed * y[i]  +  sum_{i,j} varcost[i] * x[i, j]

Constraints
-----------
(1) Demand satisfaction: for each demand type j,
        sum_{i >= j} x[i, j] >= dem[j]
    (larger-capacity containers may substitute for smaller ones).
(2) Fixed-cost linking: for each production type i,
        sum_j x[i, j] <= M * y[i]
    so the fixed cost is paid whenever type i is produced.
"""

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    "cap":     {1: 1500, 2: 2500, 3: 4000, 4: 6000, 5: 9000, 6: 12000},
    "dem":     {1: 500,  2: 550,  3: 700,  4: 900,  5: 400,  6: 300},
    "varcost": {1: 5,    2: 8,    3: 10,   4: 12,   5: 16,   6: 18},
    "fixed":   1200,
    "bigM":    100000,
}

GOLD_ANSWER = None


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    cap = d["cap"]
    dem = d["dem"]
    vc = d["varcost"]
    fixed = d["fixed"]
    bigM = d["bigM"]

    kinds = sorted(cap.keys())

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.K = pyo.Set(initialize=kinds, ordered=True)

    # Allowed (producer i, demand j) pairs: capacity_i >= capacity_j  <=>  i >= j
    allowed_pairs = [(i, j) for i in kinds for j in kinds if cap[i] >= cap[j]]
    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=allowed_pairs, dimen=2)

    # x[i,j] : units of type i produced to serve demand of type j
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.P, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # y[i] : equipment for type i is run
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.K, within=pyo.Binary)

    # (1) Demand satisfaction for each demand type j
    def demand_rule(m, j):
        return sum(m.x[i, j] for (i, jj) in m.P if jj == j) >= dem[j]
    model.demand_con = pyo.Constraint(model.K, rule=demand_rule)

    # (2) Fixed-cost linking for each production type i
    def link_rule(m, i):
        return sum(m.x[i, j] for (ii, j) in m.P if ii == i) <= bigM * m.y[i]
    model.link_con = pyo.Constraint(model.K, rule=link_rule)

    # Objective: minimize fixed + variable cost
    def obj_rule(m):
        return (sum(fixed * m.y[i] for i in m.K)
                + sum(vc[i] * m.x[i, j] for (i, j) in m.P))
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    return model

import pyomo.environ as pyo

DATA = {
    # Table 5-11 container codes 1..6
    "codes": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6],
    # Capacity (cm^3): "Capacity (cm^3) 1500 2500 4000 6000 9000 12000"
    "capacity": {1: 1500, 2: 2500, 3: 4000, 4: 6000, 5: 9000, 6: 12000},
    # Demand/units: "Demand/units 500 550 700 900 400 300"
    "demand": {1: 500, 2: 550, 3: 700, 4: 900, 5: 400, 6: 300},
    # Variable Cost (¥/unit): "Variable Cost/(¥/unit) 5 8 10 12 16 18"
    "var_cost": {1: 5, 2: 8, 3: 10, 4: 12, 5: 16, 6: 18},
    # "with a fixed cost of ¥1200"
    "fixed_cost": 1200,
    # Big-M: total demand (each unit produced can at most equal total demand)
    "bigM": 500 + 550 + 700 + 900 + 400 + 300,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA

    codes = d["codes"]
    demand = d["demand"]
    var_cost = d["var_cost"]
    fixed_cost = d["fixed_cost"]
    bigM = d["bigM"]

    # valid (i, j) pairs: type i can serve demand of type j only if capacity_i >= capacity_j
    valid_pairs = [(i, j) for i in codes for j in codes if d["capacity"][i] >= d["capacity"][j]]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.I = pyo.Set(initialize=codes, ordered=True)
    model.Pairs = pyo.Set(initialize=valid_pairs, dimen=2)

    # x[i,j]: units of type i used to satisfy demand of type j
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.Pairs, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # y[i]: equipment setup binary for type i
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.I, domain=pyo.Binary)

    # prod[i]: total units of type i produced
    model.prod = pyo.Var(model.I, domain=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # Objective: fixed setup cost + variable production cost
    def obj_rule(m):
        return (sum(fixed_cost * m.y[i] for i in m.I)
                + sum(var_cost[i] * m.prod[i] for i in m.I))
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Demand satisfaction: each demand type j fully served
    def demand_rule(m, j):
        return sum(m.x[i, j] for (i, jj) in m.Pairs if jj == j) == demand[j]
    model.demand_con = pyo.Constraint(model.I, rule=demand_rule)

    # prod[i] equals total units of type i allocated
    def prod_rule(m, i):
        return m.prod[i] == sum(m.x[i, j] for (ii, j) in m.Pairs if ii == i)
    model.prod_con = pyo.Constraint(model.I, rule=prod_rule)

    # Setup linking: production requires equipment setup
    def setup_rule(m, i):
        return m.prod[i] <= bigM * m.y[i]
    model.setup_con = pyo.Constraint(model.I, rule=setup_rule)

    return model

def build_model(data=None):

    I = d["containers"]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.I = pyo.Set(initialize=I)
    # feasible (produced type i -> demand type j) pairs with j >= i
    model.IJ = pyo.Set(
        initialize=[(i, j) for i in I for j in I if j >= i],
        dimen=2,
    )

    # x[i,j]: units of type i produced to satisfy demand of type j (j >= i)
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.IJ, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    # y[i]: 1 if dedicated equipment for type i is used
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.I, within=pyo.Binary)

    # Objective: minimize variable production cost + fixed setup cost
    def obj_rule(m):
        var = sum(d["varcost"][i] * m.x[i, j] for (i, j) in m.IJ)
        fix = sum(d["fixed_cost"] * m.y[i] for i in m.I)
        return var + fix
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Each demand j must be met by type j or any larger-capacity type i <= j
    def demand_rule(m, j):
        return sum(m.x[i, j] for i in m.I if (i, j) in m.IJ) >= d["demand"][j]
    model.demand = pyo.Constraint(model.I, rule=demand_rule)

    # Setup linking: if any type i is produced, its fixed cost applies
    def setup_rule(m, i):
        return sum(m.x[i, j] for j in m.I if (i, j) in m.IJ) <= d["bigM"][i] * m.y[i]
    model.setup = pyo.Constraint(model.I, rule=setup_rule)

    return model

import pyomo.environ as pyo

# =============================================================================
# Red Star Plastic Factory - Production / Substitution Planning (MILP)
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# DECISION VARIABLES
#   x[j]  : number of containers of type j produced (NonNegativeIntegers), j in T
#   y[j]  : 1 if type j is produced at all (Binary) -> incurs fixed cost
#   z[i,j]: number of type-j demand units satisfied by a container of type i
#           (NonNegativeIntegers), for (i,j) in A where capacity_i >= capacity_j
#
# OBJECTIVE (minimize)
#   sum_j fixed_cost * y[j] + sum_j var_cost[j] * x[j]
#
# CONSTRAINTS
#   (1) Demand satisfaction: for each j, sum over i of z[i,j] == demand[j]
#   (2) Production balance:  for each i, x[i] == sum over j of z[i,j]
#   (3) Fixed-cost linking:  x[i] <= M * y[i]  for each i
# =============================================================================

DATA = {
    "types": [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6],
    "capacity": {1: 1500, 2: 2500, 3: 4000, 4: 6000, 5: 9000, 6: 12000},
    "demand": {1: 500, 2: 550, 3: 700, 4: 900, 5: 400, 6: 300},
    "var_cost": {1: 5, 2: 8, 3: 10, 4: 12, 5: 16, 6: 18},
    "fixed_cost": 1200,
    "big_m": 100000,
}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    types = d["types"]
    capacity = d["capacity"]
    demand = d["demand"]
    var_cost = d["var_cost"]
    fixed_cost = d["fixed_cost"]
    big_m = d["big_m"]

    # Allowed substitution pairs: type i can serve demand of type j if cap_i >= cap_j
    allowed = [(i, j) for i in types for j in types if capacity[i] >= capacity[j]]

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()

    model.T = pyo.Set(initialize=types)
    model.A = pyo.Set(initialize=allowed, dimen=2)

    model.x = pyo.Var(model.T, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.T, within=pyo.Binary)
    model.z = pyo.Var(model.A, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    def obj_rule(m):
        return (
            sum(fixed_cost * m.y[i] for i in m.T)
            + sum(var_cost[i] * m.x[i] for i in m.T)
        )

    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    def demand_rule(m, j):
        return sum(m.z[i, j] for i in m.T if (i, j) in m.A) == demand[j]

    model.demand_con = pyo.Constraint(model.T, rule=demand_rule)

    def balance_rule(m, i):
        return m.x[i] == sum(m.z[i, j] for j in m.T if (i, j) in m.A)

    model.balance_con = pyo.Constraint(model.T, rule=balance_rule)

    def link_rule(m, i):
        return m.x[i] <= big_m * m.y[i]

    model.link_con = pyo.Constraint(model.T, rule=link_rule)

    return model

}


def build_model(data=None):
    d = data or DATA
    types = d["types"]
    demand = d["demand"]
    varcost = d["varcost"]
    fixed_cost = d["fixed_cost"]
    big_m = sum(demand.values())

    model = pyo.ConcreteModel()
    model.I = pyo.Set(initialize=types, ordered=True)

    # substitution pairs: j can substitute for i when capacity[j] >= capacity[i]
    pairs = [(i, j) for i in types for j in types
             if d["capacity"][j] >= d["capacity"][i]]
    model.P = pyo.Set(initialize=pairs, dimen=2, ordered=True)

    # x[i,j] = units of container j produced to meet the demand of container i
    model.x = pyo.Var(model.P, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers, bounds=(0, None))

    # y[i] = 1 if equipment for container i is switched on
    model.y = pyo.Var(model.I, within=pyo.Binary, bounds=(0, 1))

    # Objective: variable production cost + fixed equipment cost
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(
        expr=sum(varcost[j] * model.x[i, j] for (i, j) in model.P)
        + fixed_cost * sum(model.y[i] for i in model.I),
        sense=pyo.minimize,
    )

    # Each demand must be fully met (substitution allowed only upwards handled by P)
    def demand_rule(m, i):
        return sum(m.x[i, j] for (a, j) in m.P if a == i) == demand[i]
    model.demand_con = pyo.Constraint(model.I, rule=demand_rule)

    # Fixed-cost link: if any container j is produced, equipment j must be on
    def switch_rule(m, j):
        return sum((m.x[i, b] for (i, b) in m.P if b == j), 0) <= big_m * m.y[j]
    model.switch_con = pyo.Constraint(model.I, rule=switch_rule)

    return model

    model.produce = pyo.Var(model.J, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # use[i,j]: type-j containers allocated to demand type i
    model.use = pyo.Var(model.P, within=pyo.NonNegativeIntegers)

    # setup[j]: equipment for type j activated
    model.setup = pyo.Var(model.J, within=pyo.Binary)

    # Objective: variable production cost + fixed activation cost
    def obj_rule(m):
        var_total = sum(var_cost[j] * m.produce[j] for j in m.J)
        fixed_total = sum(fixed_cost * m.setup[j] for j in m.J)
        return var_total + fixed_total
    model.obj = pyo.Objective(rule=obj_rule, sense=pyo.minimize)

    # Each demand type i must be fully satisfied by some allowed container type
    def demand_rule(m, i):
        return sum(m.use[i, j] for j in m.J if (i, j) in m.P) == demand[i]
    model.demand_sat = pyo.Constraint(model.I, rule=demand_rule)

    # Production of type j equals total units of type j allocated
    def link_rule(m, j):
        return sum(m.use[i, j] for i in m.I if (i, j) in m.P) == m.produce[j]
    model.prod_link = pyo.Constraint(model.J, rule=link_rule)

    # Activation: produce[j] <= big_m * setup[j]
    def setup_rule(m, j):
        return m.produce[j] <= big_m * m.setup[j]
    model.activation = pyo.Constraint(model.J, rule=setup_rule)

    return model
